pairs.why: A keeps the real card's flat wall-mounted front view with a soft drop shadow on the stripes, while B sets the clock on a floor with a horizon line, which gives it a different ground plane and viewpoint.
B has a big hero seen from slightly below and close up, with the truss cropped at the frame edge, like the real card's near camera. A has a small, distant fixture floating in the background.
Both show the same 3/4 high view, the same mild perspective and the same lunar ground plane, so the camera gives no reason to choose.
B shows a tilted top face with visible side thickness at the bottom edge, like the real card's raised 3/4 view. A looks almost like a flat front-on icon.
A is a flat frontal view with weak convergence, like the real card's straight-on door. B adds more door-frame depth and step perspective.
B shows a hint of the floor plane and a slightly turned head, which reads closer to the real card's receding railing and top-down glimpse. A is rigidly frontal.
A has the visor turned toward the front-left and the cap sitting on receding floorboards at a similar angle to the real card. B is turned slightly differently, with a flatter side view.
Both put a frontal palm on a low dune with a similar backdrop and similar mild perspective, and neither is clearly nearer the real card's depth layering.
